objective: Implement periodic worker review and evidence-based hang investigation over the verified CW-10 active-run/session/exit boundaries.

dependencies.CW-05: AutomationState and observation port contracts are available in src/workbench/contracts/ports_v2.py

required_behavior: Use an explicit clock/tick seam. While automation is active and a run is active, make a worker model review due every 60 seconds; do not impose a fixed lifetime count cap.

When worker/model transport is busy or user conversation/composer/approval input has priority, retain only the newest due review, expose delayed/coalesced status, and dispatch it when safe. User interaction always wins.

During local pause/cancel/unapproved/unhealthy state, do not start a new model review, but continue non-model log/process/exit collection and immediately surface confirmed exit events. CW-12 owns actual manager abort/reconcile integration.
Silence and elapsed time alone must never classify hang or exit. Hang investigation must report explicit process/lifecycle evidence, unknowns, and suggested next observations.
Prove the 121st periodic review and 13th normal peer wake execute; usage has no fixed cap and distinguishes observed, estimated, and unknown values.
Consume active run/session/exit facts through narrow ports/callables; do not bypass CW-10 public response/authority contracts or persist model text/secrets.
verification: Deterministic clock tests for exact 60-second boundaries, long-run 121 checks, 13 peer wakes, busy latest-one coalescing, user-priority delay, pause behavior, immediate exit, silence/hang evidence, usage labels.
Actual OMP 18.2.10 review path with bounded cleanup and no private provider state; relevant CW-10 workflow/bridge regressions.
